notes.title: A release is an execution, not a legal opinion
notes.content: HIM verifies the requester, authority, record scope, date range, format, fee rule and destination. Privacy or Legal resolves disputed authority. The release record must show exactly what left, when, to whom and under which verified basis; a signed-looking document is not enough by itself.

notes.title: Patient amendment workflow
notes.content: A patient may challenge information without asking HIM to silently rewrite a clinician's record. The workflow records the request, routes the disputed entry to the responsible author or authorised clinical reviewer, preserves the original, records acceptance or denial, and sends the required response and downstream notice.

notes.title: Subpoena and court-order distinction
notes.content: The team must not treat every subpoena, warrant and court order as interchangeable. Log the issuing body, jurisdiction, service method, deadline and requested categories, preserve the request, and route interpretation to counsel before producing anything beyond a clearly authorised path.

notes.title: Minimum necessary release package
notes.content: For an authorised disclosure, export only the approved record types and dates. Exclude internal audit metadata, unrelated encounters, psychotherapy notes and specially protected content unless the verified authority explicitly reaches them. A broad export is not a safer operational shortcut.

notes.title: Record-merge correction
notes.content: When two identities or encounters were merged incorrectly, correcting the EHR display is only one step. HIM needs an authoritative identity decision, Informatics needs downstream-system impact, Integration needs message replay or correction status, and Privacy needs an assessment of any disclosure to the wrong chart.

notes.title: Portal proxy access
notes.content: A family relationship does not create portal access. Verify the patient or legal representative, the scope and expiry of the proxy, any age or service-specific restriction, and the revocation path. The access decision must not be inferred from who usually attends appointments.

notes.title: Release quality check
notes.content: Before transmission, use a second-person check for patient identity, requester, destination, date range and excluded categories when the request is high risk. After transmission, retain the manifest and delivery confirmation without copying the entire disclosed record into general work notes.

notes.title: HIM coverage boundary
notes.content: Routine record requests are a business-hours queue. Urgent care access stays with the clinical EHR and care team; urgent legal demands use the published HIM and counsel escalation route. Alicia's personal calendar is not the health system's twenty-four-hour coverage model.
